metadata.title: COBO L1 Linux Endpoint SSPP
metadata.remarks: Operating system–specific System Security and Privacy Plan defining how Linux endpoints implement the COBO L1 baseline endpoint trust tier.

import-profile.remarks: Institutional security and privacy baseline profile.

system-characteristics.system-description: A Linux workstation configured and managed to meet the baseline COBO L1 institutional endpoint trust requirements for general-purpose institutional workloads.

props.name: inherits-from-sspp
props.remarks: This Linux SSPP inherits all trust requirements from the COBO L1 Endpoint SSPP.

props.name: supported-distributions
props.remarks: Only institution-approved, vendor-supported long-term support (LTS) Linux distributions are permitted.

props.name: ownership-model
props.remarks: Linux endpoint is owned by the institution.

props.name: management-model
props.remarks: Linux endpoint is centrally enrolled, configured, and monitored using institutional management tooling.

props.name: cryptographic-identity
props.remarks: Linux endpoint identity must use TPM-backed non-exportable private keys and PKI-issued device certificates.

props.name: cryptographic-compliance
props.remarks: Linux cryptographic subsystems must operate using FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic modules.

props.name: secure-boot
props.remarks: UEFI Secure Boot must be enabled and enforced.

props.name: full-disk-encryption
props.remarks: Full disk encryption must be enabled using approved cryptographic mechanisms.

props.name: baseline-hardening
props.remarks: Linux configuration applies CIS Linux Benchmark Level 1 settings appropriate for workstation use.

props.name: mandatory-access-controls
props.remarks: Mandatory access controls (e.g., SELinux or AppArmor) must be enabled and enforcing.

props.name: malware-and-threat-protection
props.remarks: Institution-approved endpoint threat protection and integrity monitoring must be enabled.

props.name: posture-and-health-reporting
props.remarks: Linux endpoints continuously report health and compliance posture to Secure Endpoint consumers.

props.name: eligible-data-classifications
props.remarks: Linux COBO L1 endpoints may participate in workflows involving Data Classification Levels 1 and 2.

props.name: non-equivalence-statement
props.remarks: Endpoint assurance does not grant automatic entitlement to any data classification.

props.name: lifecycle-governance
props.remarks: Linux endpoints must support Secure Endpoint lifecycle workflows including enrollment, suspension, recovery, and retirement.

system-implementation.remarks: This SSPP defines how Linux endpoints implement COBO L1 trust requirements through secure boot, TPM-backed identity, hardened configuration, and centralized management.

control-implementation.remarks: Linux security baselines, configuration management, bootloader configuration, TPM integration, and CIS-aligned hardening implement this SSPP and are maintained as version-controlled implementation artifacts.
